1: # OpenGlimpse — Project Documentation
2: # SCCCI Delegation Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance System
3: # Problem Statement #10 | 4-Person Team
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Project Overview
8: 
9: SCCCI (Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce & Industry) manages overseas business delegations of 15–30 (sometimes 100+) participants across multiple coaches and venues. Currently, headcount is taken manually by counting heads and doing roll calls — a slow, error-prone process that causes anxiety and programme overruns when someone is missing.
10: 
11: This system digitises and accelerates that process using a React-based mobile-first application with facial recognition as the primary attendance mechanism, supplemented by QR code scanning as a backup.
12: 
13: ---
14: 
15: ## 2. Use Case Definition
16: 
17: ### 2.1 Primary Use Case
18: **Title:** Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance with Multi-Staff Sync
19: 
20: **Goal:** Allow SCCCI secretariat staff to take attendance for an overseas delegation in under 1 minute (30 pax) or 2 minutes (100+ pax) using facial recognition, with instant visibility of who is present or absent — across multiple staff devices simultaneously.
21: 
22: **Actors:**
23: - Staff / Secretariat (Primary) — takes attendance using facial recognition; can manually confirm identity if needed
24: - Trip Manager / Admin (Primary) — creates programmes, assigns staff, views consolidated real-time attendance, confirms departure readiness
25: - Delegate (Secondary) — identified via facial recognition as they enter coaches or venues
26: 
27: ### 2.2 Preconditions
28: - A programme has been created with a predetermined participant list
29: - Each delegate's facial photograph has been registered in the system (passport-sized photo)
30: - At least one staff member has the app open, is logged in, and is assigned to the current programme/route
31: - Internet connectivity (cellular data or hotspot) is available at the location for real-time cloud sync
32: - For first login by staff, updated facial photo is required to verify identity
33: 
34: ### 2.3 Main Flow (Happy Path)
35: 1. Admin creates a new programme with routes, bus assignments, and participant list.
36: 2. Staff member logs in with their account (verified by facial recognition on first login).
37: 3. Staff opens the attendance marking screen for their assigned route/coach.
38: 4. Delegate boards; staff activates live camera with facial detection. App displays bounding boxes around detected faces in real time.
39: 5. App matches detected face against stored delegate embeddings. If match confidence is high, delegate is marked Present automatically.
40: 6. If confidence is low or face is unrecognised, admin receives in-app alert. Staff can manually confirm identity from the list or use QR code backup.
41: 7. Attendance record syncs instantly to the cloud. All staff devices update in real time.
42: 8. The dashboard shows: Present list (with photos), Unidentified/Absent list (highlighted at top), and Ready-to-Depart status.
43: 9. When all delegates are accounted for, the Trip Manager confirms departure readiness.
44: 
45: ### 2.4 Alternative & Exception Flows
46: 
47: **Alt A — Low confidence facial match:**
48: - App flags confidence score and shows top candidate matches.
49: - Staff taps to confirm or manually selects from the list.
50: - Fallback: QR code scan on separate tab if delegate has badge.
51: 
52: **Alt B — Unidentified face:**
53: - Admin receives in-app alert for faces that don't match any registered delegate.
54: - Staff can manually add the person if it's a new arrival or late joiner.
55: - Photo quality may be poor — staff can request re-scan or use QR/manual override.
56: 
57: **Alt C — Manual attendance override:**
58: - Staff can always tap a delegate's name from the list to mark them Present or Absent.
59: - Covers roll calls when facial recognition is not available or delegate forgot badge.
60: 
61: **Alt D — Delegate joins/leaves programme mid-journey:**
62: - Admin amends the programme participant list on-the-fly from the app (add/remove delegate, change route/coach assignment).
63: 
64: **Alt E — Offline when scanning:**
65: - App queues facial scans locally (face image + embedding) if internet drops.
66: - When connectivity restores, queued scans are sent to backend for processing.
67: - Cloud data merges offline scans without loss or duplication.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. System Requirements (Prioritised)
72: 
73: P1 = must-have MVP; P2 = high value, build after P1; P3 = nice-to-have.
74: 
75: | Pri. | Requirement | Owner |
76: |------|-------------|-------|
77: | P1 | Facial recognition with real-time face detection — bounding boxes drawn around faces in camera view | Ryan |
78: | P1 | Face embedding generation & storage — store delegate faces as embeddings in PostgreSQL | Ryan + Backend |
79: | P1 | Manual identity confirmation — staff can manually tap delegate name to override low-confidence matches | Ryan / XY |
80: | P1 | Offline sync queue — frontend buffers facial scans locally; backend processes & merges on reconnect | Rayhan |
81: | P1 | Real-time attendance dashboard with present/absent/unidentified lists; missing marked at top | XY |
82: | P1 | Multi-staff cloud sync — all staff see the same attendance in real time across devices | Backend + Ryan |
83: | P1 | Programme & route creation — admin can set up trips, assign buses/routes, manage participant lists | XY / Matt |
84: | P1 | Staff account management — admin CRUD operations, staff login, face verification on first login | Matt |
85: | P1 | In-app alerts for unidentified faces — admin notified of FR matches below confidence threshold | Ryan / Backend |
86: | P1 | China-accessible hosting — app must not be blocked by Great Firewall | Backend |
87: | P2 | QR code backup scanning — delegate has QR on badge; staff can switch tab to scan if FR not possible | Ryan |
88: | P2 | Attendance summary & data aggregation — totals, pass rates, missing delegates report | XY |
89: | P2 | Ready-to-depart indicator — admin confirms all delegates accounted for before departure | XY |
90: | P2 | In-app chat & announcements — team members can communicate; announce updates with reactions | Rayhan |
91: | P2 | Navbar navigation — easy routing between Programme, Attendance, Profile, Chat sections | Rayhan |
92: | P3 | User profile management — staff can update personal info including new facial photo | Matt |
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 4. Tech Stack Details
97: 
98: ### 4.1 Frontend
99: - React web application with responsive design — optimised for staff smartphones and tablets
100: - Facial recognition: face-api.js library for real-time face detection, embedding generation, and similarity matching
101: - Camera API: device camera access with live face detection and bounding box visualization
102: - QR code scanner: separate tab with camera-based QR decoding (backup mode)
103: - Offline queue: browser localStorage for queuing facial scans and embeddings when disconnected
104: - UI: simple, high-contrast, glanceable — unidentified/absent delegates surfaced at top of list
105: 
106: ### 4.2 Backend
107: - Node.js REST API (Express.js) for programmes, routes, attendance, user management, and chat
108: - Real-time sync: WebSockets (Socket.io) for instant multi-device attendance updates and in-app chat
109: - Database: PostgreSQL — stores programmes, participants, facial embeddings (vectors), scan events, chat messages, user accounts
110: - Offline queue processing: backend receives offline scans, validates embeddings, and merges with live data without duplication
111: - Auth: staff login via JWT; delegate identity verified by facial embedding similarity
112: - Hosting: must be accessible from China — Alibaba Cloud (Singapore/Hong Kong region) strongly preferred
113: 
114: ### 4.3 Data & Privacy
115: - Delegate data: name, facial photograph (passport-sized JPEG), optional QR code ID, optional NFC tag ID
116: - Facial embeddings: stored in PostgreSQL as numeric vectors (face-api.js output); compared for similarity matching
117: - Staff data: account credentials, facial photo for login verification, permission levels
118: - Photos pre-registered by admin before the programme; staff updates own photo on first login
119: - Chat messages: retained for programme history; can be archived per admin policy
120: 
121: ### 4.4 Offline Sync Engine
122: 
123: #### Architecture
124: - **Client:** Dexie.js (IndexedDB) with `requestCache` and `pendingChanges` tables
125: - **Interception layer:** `services/api.js` `request()` caches GET responses; offline reads serve from cache, offline writes queue `{ method, path, body, token }` to `pendingChanges`
126: - **Auth endpoints:** `/api/auth` in `SYNC_PREFIXES`; login excluded via `NEVER_QUEUE`; token carried in ops for auth writes
127: - **Sync trigger:** `hooks/useSync.js` calls `sync/changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, and tab `focus`; dispatches `sync:done` custom event after successful sync
128: - **Server:** `POST /sync` registered in `index.js` via `registerSyncRoutes(app)`; handled by `modules/sync/syncController.js` which replays ops against Sequelize models; auth ops validated via `parseToken()` + DB lookup
129: - **Vite proxy:** `/sync` added to `vite.config.js` proxy table so `changeHandler` fetch reaches Express (was root cause of silent sync failure)
130: - **Synced entity types:** programme, route, delegate, attendance, readyToDepart, auth (prefixed `/programmes`, `/delegates`, or `/api/auth`)
131: - **Not synced:** login (`/api/auth/login`), face recognition, QR scanning, chat, users (`/users`)
132: 
133: #### Client-side data flow
134: - `request()` in `api.js` checks `navigator.onLine`:
135:   - **Online:** fetch from server; cache GET responses in `requestCache` for synced paths
136:   - **Offline:** GET reads from `requestCache`; POST/PUT/DELETE pushes to `pendingChanges` and returns optimistic result (`{ ...body, id: 'pending' }`)
137: - **Components show optimistic data immediately via `setAccounts` (local state)** — `handleCreate`, `handleUpdate`, `handleDelete` in `ParticipantManagement.jsx` skip the stale cache and directly update state when offline
138: - **Offline-disabled UIs:** CameraPage capture/confirm buttons disabled; ChatInput shows "unavailable" placeholder; face upload skipped in ParticipantManagement
139: 
140: #### Sync lifecycle
141: 1. **Queue:** offline writes accumulate in `pendingChanges` (IndexedDB, persists across sessions)
142: 2. **Trigger:** `useSync.js` fires `changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, or tab `focus` (with ref guard to prevent concurrent runs)
143: 3. **Send:** `changeHandler()` does `POST /sync` with `{ ops, timestamp }`; on 200 OK, deletes `pendingChanges` and dispatches `sync:done`
144: 4. **Server processing:** `syncController.js` `HANDLERS` map dispatches each op by `method + path` pattern; auth ops include `validateToken()` checks
145: 5. **UI refresh:** components listen for `sync:done` via `window.addEventListener('sync:done', ...)` and `sync:done` event to re-fetch fresh data: `ParticipantManagement.jsx`, `ProgrammePage.jsx`, `directory.jsx`
146: 6. **Connectivity indicator:** `useConnectivity.js` polls `pendingChanges` every 3s **and** listens for `sync:done` to instantly update `pendingCount`; camera & chat disabled when offline
147: 
148: ### 4.5 Hardware (for Demo & Production)
149: - Development: laptop webcam acceptable with printed QR codes and mock data
150: - Final demo: mobile phone (Android/iOS) for live facial recognition, camera-based QR scanning
151: - QR badges: printed QR codes embedded in delegate badge lanyard
152: - NFC badges: optional for future enhancement; requires NFC-equipped phone
153: 
154: ---
155: 
156: ## 5. Integration Points
157: 
158: - Ryan calls: `POST /programmes/{id}/scans` with facial embedding + confidence
159: - XY calls: `PUT /programmes/{id}/attendance/{delegateId}` for manual mark present/absent
160: - Ryan & XY listen: WebSocket event `attendance:updated` to refresh dashboard in real time
161: - Rayhan manages: offline queue — client-side buffers scan payloads, backend deduplicates on sync
162: - Matt ensures: JWT tokens issued by auth endpoint are validated by all API consumers
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## 6. Success Criteria
167: 
168: | Metric | Target |
169: |--------|--------|
170: | Time to reconcile 30 pax | < 1 minute |
171: | Time to reconcile 100+ pax | < 2 minutes |
172: | Facial recognition accuracy | ≥99% with staff confirmation for matches |
173: | Data loss on offline sync | Zero |
174: | Staff usability score | ≥4.5 / 5 |
175: | China accessibility | Fully functional on Alibaba Cloud; no GFW blocks |
176: | Cloud sync latency | < 2 seconds for multi-device updates |
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## 7. Out of Scope
181: 
182: - Real-time location tracking or GPS maps (client uses WhatsApp)
183: - Liveness detection / anti-spoofing (client prioritises speed over security compliance)
184: - Government compliance audit trails
185: - Integration with external HR, CRM, or event management systems
186: - Push notifications beyond in-app alerts
187: - Voice calls or video conferencing (WhatsApp remains communication channel)
188: 
189: ---
190: 
191: ## 8. Assumptions & Risks
192: 
193: ### 8.1 Assumptions
194: - Internet (cellular data or hotspot) is available at all trip locations (China, ASEAN countries)
195: - Client will provide sample participant data: names + passport-sized facial photos
196: - Staff members have smartphones capable of running React web app (Android/iOS, modern browsers)
197: - Face-api.js embeddings are sufficient for matching with ≥99% accuracy among diverse delegate faces
198: - PostgreSQL with pgvector extension (or JSONB) is available on hosting provider
199: 
200: ### 8.2 Risks & Mitigation
201: 
202: | Risk | Mitigation |
203: |------|------------|
204: | Facial recognition accuracy on diverse faces, varied lighting, or poor photo quality | Set clear confidence thresholds (0.6+); always offer manual override; test with diverse delegation photos early |
205: | Great Firewall blocks Alibaba Cloud or host provider | Verify Alibaba Cloud Singapore/HK region connectivity from China SIM in Week 1; have AWS HK as backup |
206: | Face-api.js embedding format incompatible with backend matching algorithm | Agree on embedding format (size, normalization) in Week 1; test sample embeddings on both sides |
207: | WebSocket scaling — many concurrent staff devices cause latency | Load test early; consider Socket.io room/namespace for per-programme isolation |
208: | Offline queue duplication — same scan synced twice on reconnect | Add unique scan ID (timestamp + device ID) to each offline queue item; backend deduplicates on ID |
209: | QR code as backup underutilised if FR works well | Defer QR printing to P2; clients may choose not to use if FR is reliable |
210: 
211: ---
212: 
213: ## 9. Pages (UI)
214: 
215: - **Dashboard / Overview** — instant snapshot of delegate status; real-time counter (present/overall)
216: - **Scanner** — QR/NFC and facial scanning
217: - **Profile Page** — CRUD operations for delegate profiles
218: - **Support Tickets** — CRUD operations
219: - **Directory** — all delegates' name and info; manual check-in; notes (badge missing, verified manually)
220: - **Missing List** — shows who is missing; call button for direct contact; toggle for special occasions
221: - **Sync Log** — connectivity indicator (offline/online/syncing); pending sync count

380: ProgrammeDelegate.addDelegates = async function (programmeId, body) {
381:   const { delegates, delegateIds, delegateId, name, badge, routeId, userIds } = body;
382:   const addToRoute = async (did) => {
383:     if (routeId) {
384:       // One route per delegate: move, don't duplicate
385:       await RouteMember.destroy({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: did } });
386:       await RouteMember.findOrCreate({ where: { routeId, delegateId: did, programmeId }, defaults: { routeId, delegateId: did, programmeId } });
387:     }
388:   };
389:   // New: accept userIds — find-or-create delegates by userId
390:   if (userIds && Array.isArray(userIds)) {
391:     const added = [];
392:     for (const uid of userIds) {
393:       let del = await Delegate.findOne({ where: { userId: uid } });
394:       if (!del) {
395:         const u = await user.findByPk(uid);
396:         if (!u) continue;
397:         del = await Delegate.create({ name: u.enName, userId: uid });
398:       }
399:       await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id } });
400:       await addToRoute(del.id);
401:       added.push({ delegateId: del.id, name: del.name });
402:     }
403:     return added;
404:   }
405:   if (delegates && Array.isArray(delegates)) {
406:     const added = [];
407:     for (const d of delegates) {
408:       const [del] = await Delegate.findOrCreate({ where: { name: d.name }, defaults: { name: d.name, badge: d.badge || null } });
409:       await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id } });
410:       await addToRoute(del.id);
411:       added.push({ delegateId: del.id, name: del.name });
412:     }
413:     return added;
414:   }
415:   if (delegateIds && Array.isArray(delegateIds)) {
416:     for (const id of delegateIds) {
417:       await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: id }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId: id } });
418:       await addToRoute(id);
419:     }
420:     return delegateIds.map((id) => ({ delegateId: id }));
421:   }
422:   if (delegateId) {
423:     await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId } });
424:     await addToRoute(delegateId);
425:     return [{ delegateId }];
426:   }
427:   if (name) {
428:     const del = await Delegate.create({ name, badge: badge || null });
429:     await ProgrammeDelegate.create({ programmeId, delegateId: del.id });
430:     await addToRoute(del.id);
431:     return [{ delegateId: del.id, name }];
432:   }
433:   throw new Error("Provide delegates array, delegateIds, delegateId, or name");
434: };

text:
Added WhatsApp-style emoji reactions to the chat. Here's what changed:

**Server**
- `database/db.cjs`: new `MessageReaction` model (`message_reactions` table, unique per message+user, cascade-deletes with messages) + associations.
- `database/dbcrudmethods.js`: new `Reactions` CRUD class.
- `modules/chat/chatserver.cjs`: messages now include `id` and grouped `reactions`; new `react` socket event that toggles/sets one reaction per user per message and broadcasts `reaction:update`.

**Client**
- `pages/chat/ReactionBar.jsx` (new): quick-reaction bar with 👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏.
- `pages/chat/chatbubble.jsx`: hover (desktop) or long-press (mobile) opens the reaction bar; reaction pills shown below the bubble with counts, your own highlighted; tapping a pill toggles/switches your reaction.
- `pages/chat/chat.jsx`: listens for `reaction:update` and emits `react`.
- `index.css`: styles for the bar and reaction pills.

Usage: hover or long-press a message → pick an emoji. Tap a reaction pill to remove/change yours. Reactions persist in Postgres and sync live across devices (table auto-created on server start via `sequelize.sync`).

5: const SYNC_PREFIXES = ['/programmes', '/delegates', '/api/auth', '/api/user', '/users'];
6: //prevents auth login from being queued for sync
7: const NEVER_QUEUE = ['/api/auth/login'];
8: 
9: function isSynced(path) {
10:   //check if path is in NEVER_QUEUE
11:   if (NEVER_QUEUE.some(p => path.startsWith(p))) return false;
12:   return SYNC_PREFIXES.some(p => path.startsWith(p));
13: }

15: //handle requests from client
16: async function request(method, path, body, token) {
17:   const opts = {
18:     method,
19:     headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
20:   };
21:   //check for token
22:   if (token) {
23:     opts.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
24:   }
25:   if (body !== undefined) {
26:     opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);
27:   }
28: //client action if online
29:   if (navigator.onLine) {
30:     try {
31:       const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}${path}`, opts);
32:       if (res.status === 204) {
33:         return null;
34:       }
35:       const text = await res.text();
36:       if (!text) {
37:         if (!res.ok) {
38:           throw new Error(`Request failed (${res.status})`);
39:         }
40:         return null;
41:       }
42:       let data;
43:       try {
44:         data = JSON.parse(text);
45:       } catch {
46:         data = null;
47:       }
48:       if (!res.ok) {
49:         throw new Error(data?.error || `Request failed (${res.status})`);
50:       }
51:       if (method === 'GET' && data !== null && isSynced(path)) {
52:         await db.requestCache.put({
53:           path: path.split('?')[0],
54:           data
55:         });
56:       }
57:       return data;
58:       //if client is offline
59:     } catch (err) {
60:       //(unlikely case here) if sync path does not exist(ie does not support offline sync)
61:       if (!isSynced(path)) {
62:         throw err;
63:       }
64:     }
65:   }
66: //check if cached data exists
67:   if (!isSynced(path)) {
68:     throw new Error('Network required');
69:   }
70: //handle get requests
71:   if (method === 'GET') {
72:     const cached = await db.requestCache.get(path.split('?')[0]);
73:     if (!cached) {
74:       throw new Error('Not available offline');

1: # Event Management App — Redesign Spec
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document is a redesign and UX-optimization spec for an existing event management app. Read this fully before touching code. Study the current codebase and user flow first, then implement. Do not change the tech stack: JSX + Tailwind CSS remain as-is. This is a visual and interaction redesign plus a UX pass on the existing flows, not a rewrite of business logic.
6: 
7: ## Step 0: Study Before Building
8: 
9: Before writing any code:
10: 
11: 1. Map every screen currently in the app (auth, dashboard, event list, event detail, create/edit event, RSVP/attendee views, settings, etc).
12: 2. Trace the full user flow: sign in/sign up -> dashboard -> browse/search events -> create event -> edit event -> delete event -> view event detail -> RSVP or manage attendees -> sign out.
13: 3. For each CRUD action, identify where the flow currently has friction: extra taps, unclear states, missing feedback (loading, empty, error, success), dead ends, or inconsistent navigation.
14: 4. Write a short internal list of the friction points you find and the fix you're applying for each. Keep this list as PR/commit notes, not as a separate doc.
15: 5. Only after this audit, begin implementation.
16: 
17: Optimize the flow itself where it's clearly broken (e.g. no confirmation on delete, no empty states, unclear save/cancel affordances, sign-in requiring too many steps). Don't invent new features outside CRUD + auth + navigation scope.
18: 
19: ## Design Principles
20: 
21: - Mobile-first. Design and build for a ~390px viewport first, then scale up. Every screen must be fully usable one-handed.
22: - Modern, minimal, functional. No decoration that doesn't serve a purpose.
23: - Grounded in Material Design principles: clear elevation/hierarchy, purposeful motion, consistent touch targets (min 44px), predictable component behavior.
24: - Favor whitespace and typographic hierarchy over borders and boxes to separate content.
25: - Every interactive element gives feedback: pressed state, loading state, disabled state.
26: 
27: ## What to Avoid (explicit anti-patterns)
28: 
29: - No purple gradients or generic "AI app" gradient backgrounds.
30: - No default/overused font pairings (no default Inter-only look with no hierarchy). Pick a deliberate type pairing (see Typography).
31: - No inline styles (`style={{...}}`) anywhere in JSX. All styling lives in Tailwind utility classes composed via `@apply` in `index.css`.
32: - No top navbar on mobile. Replace with the floating bottom navbar described below.
33: - No overly stylized code comments. No em dashes in comments. No long docstrings/JSDoc essays. Comments are short, plain, functional labels, e.g.:
34:   - `// Offline sync banner`
35:   - `// Navbar`
36:   - `// Dashboard create button`
37:   - `// RSVP toggle`
38: 
39: ## Color System (Black & Blue)
40: 
41: Define these as CSS custom properties in `index.css` and map them into `tailwind.config` theme colors. Keep it a tight palette, not a rainbow of shades.
42: 
43: - Background base: near-black, e.g. `#0B0D10` / `#111418`
44: - Surface (cards, sheets): slightly lifted dark, e.g. `#171A1F`
45: - Primary accent (blue): a single confident blue, e.g. `#3B82F6` or a deeper `#2563EB`, used for primary actions, active nav icon, focus rings
46: - Secondary accent: a muted steel-blue or blue-gray for secondary elements, e.g. `#4B5563`/`#64748B`
47: - Text primary: off-white, e.g. `#F5F7FA` (never pure `#FFFFFF` on pure black — soften both ends)
48: - Text secondary/muted: gray-blue, e.g. `#8B93A1`
49: - Success / error / warning: keep desaturated, consistent with the dark theme (muted green, muted red, muted amber) — not neon.
50: - Dividers/borders: low-opacity white or blue, e.g. `rgba(255,255,255,0.06)`
51: 
52: Avoid pure black (`#000`) and pure white (`#FFF`) as primary surfaces — both read as flat/cheap. Use near-black and off-white instead.
53: 
54: ## Typography
55: 
56: - Pick one primary sans-serif for UI text (e.g. Manrope, General Sans, Satoshi, or similar — avoid defaulting to plain Inter with no weight variation) and use weight (500/600/700) to build hierarchy instead of introducing a second family for body text.
57: - Optional: a distinct display weight/family only for large headers (dashboard title, event titles) if it adds character — keep it subtle, not decorative.
58: - Type scale (mobile): 
59:   - Display/H1: 24–28px, semibold
60:   - H2/section: 18–20px, semibold
61:   - Body: 15–16px, regular/medium
62:   - Caption/meta: 13px, medium, muted color
63: - Line height generous enough for readability on small screens (1.4–1.6 for body).
64: 
65: ## Navigation: Floating Pill Bottom Navbar
66: 
67: - Fixed to the bottom of the viewport, floating with margin from screen edges (not flush/full-width), rounded-full (`rounded-full` pill shape).
68: - Elevated with a soft shadow and a slightly translucent/blurred surface (`backdrop-blur`) over the dark background.
69: - 4–5 icon-only or icon+micro-label tabs max: Dashboard, Events, Create, Notifications/Activity, Profile (adjust to match actual app sections — don't invent sections that don't exist).
70: - Active tab: filled icon + blue accent color + subtle background pill behind the icon.
71: - Inactive tabs: outlined/stroke icon style, muted text-secondary color.
72: - Use a modern icon set already available in the project's dependencies (e.g. `lucide-react`) — outline style icons, consistent stroke width.
73: - Center "Create" action can be visually emphasized (raised circle, solid accent fill) if that matches the primary CRUD action of the app.
74: - Navbar sits above content with enough bottom padding on scrollable pages so content never hides behind it.
75: - No top navbar on mobile breakpoints. A minimal top bar (page title + contextual action, e.g. back button or search) is acceptable only where needed, but primary navigation lives in the bottom pill bar.
76: 
77: ## Buttons & Interaction Feedback
78: 
79: - All buttons must have a visible pressed/active state (e.g. `active:scale-[0.97]`) and a smooth transition (`transition-transform duration-150 ease-out` or similar) — define these as reusable `@apply` classes, not repeated inline utility strings.
80: - Primary buttons: solid blue fill, off-white text, rounded (not full-pill for rectangular buttons — reserve full pill shape for the navbar and small tags/chips), subtle shadow on rest, slightly deeper shadow or scale-down on press.
81: - Secondary/ghost buttons: transparent or low-opacity surface fill, blue or white text, visible border or subtle surface tint.
82: - Destructive actions (delete event, remove attendee): muted red, always behind a confirmation step (sheet or dialog), never a single accidental tap.
83: - Disabled state: reduced opacity + `cursor-not-allowed`, no pointer feedback.
84: - Loading state on async actions (save, delete, sign in): inline spinner or skeleton, button disabled while pending, no layout shift.
85: - Use CSS transitions/transforms for all micro-interactions. Avoid heavy animation libraries unless already in the stack; keep motion under ~200ms for taps, ~250–300ms for sheet/modal transitions.
86: 
87: ## Layout & Components
88: 
89: - Cards (event cards, list items): rounded corners (`rounded-2xl`/`rounded-xl`), dark surface color, subtle border or shadow for separation, generous internal padding, no nested boxes-within-boxes.
90: - Forms (create/edit event): mobile-first single column, large touch-friendly inputs, floating or top-aligned labels (avoid placeholder-only labels), clear sticky save/cancel action at the bottom on small screens.
91: - Empty states: every list (events, attendees, notifications) needs a designed empty state — icon + short message + primary action if relevant. Never a blank screen.
92: - Loading states: skeleton placeholders matching the shape of the content that will load, not a generic spinner for full-page loads.
93: - Error states: inline, human-readable, with a retry action where applicable.
94: - Modals/sheets: use bottom sheets on mobile for actions like create/edit/confirm-delete rather than centered modals, since this matches thumb-reach and mobile-first patterns.
95: - Consistent spacing scale: stick to Tailwind's default spacing scale (4px increments); don't introduce arbitrary pixel values unless unavoidable.
96: 
97: ## Responsiveness
98: 
99: - Build mobile-first (no `sm:`/base styles targeting desktop first). Base classes = mobile. Use `md:`/`lg:` to progressively enhance for tablet/desktop.
100: - On larger viewports, the floating bottom navbar can either remain (common in modern apps) or convert to a compact side rail — pick one and apply it consistently; don't revert to a legacy top navbar.
101: - Test at minimum: 375px, 390px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px.
102: 
103: ## CSS Architecture Rules
104: 
105: - No inline styles (`style={{}}`) anywhere in JSX.
106: - No ad hoc long utility strings repeated across components. Where a class combination is reused 2+ times (buttons, cards, inputs, nav items), extract it into `index.css` using Tailwind's `@apply`, e.g.:
107: 
108: ```css
109: /* index.css */
110: .btn-primary {
111:   @apply bg-blue-600 text-slate-50 rounded-xl px-5 py-3 font-medium transition-transform duration-150 ease-out active:scale-[0.97] disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed;
112: }
113: 
114: .nav-pill {
115:   @apply fixed bottom-4 left-4 right-4 flex items-center justify-around rounded-full bg-surface/80 backdrop-blur-md shadow-lg py-3;
116: }
117: 
118: .card {
119:   @apply rounded-2xl bg-surface p-4 border border-white/5;
120: }
121: ```
122: 
123: - JSX components then reference these classes directly (`className="btn-primary"`), composing with a few one-off utility classes only when truly one-off.
124: - Keep `index.css` organized in clear sections with plain comments: base, typography, buttons, nav, cards, forms, states (loading/empty/error).
125: - Define the color palette as CSS variables at the top of `index.css` (`:root { --bg: ...; --surface: ...; --accent: ...; }`) and reference them in `tailwind.config.js` theme extension so both Tailwind classes and raw CSS stay in sync.
126: 
127: ## Code Comment Style
128: 
129: - Short, plain, functional. Describe what the block does, not why in essay form.
130: - Good: `// Create event form`, `// RSVP button`, `// Empty state for no events`
131: - Bad: long paragraph docstrings, em dashes, marketing-style phrasing ("This beautifully handles...").
132: - Comment only non-obvious logic; skip comments on self-explanatory JSX.
133: 
134: ## Deliverable Checklist for the Agent
135: 
136: - [ ] Full user flow audited (sign in through all CRUD actions) with friction points fixed
137: - [ ] Bottom floating pill navbar implemented, replacing any top nav on mobile
138: - [ ] Black/blue palette applied consistently via CSS variables + Tailwind theme
139: - [ ] Typography hierarchy applied, no default unstyled text
140: - [ ] All buttons have press feedback, loading state, disabled state
141: - [ ] No inline styles; shared styles moved to `index.css` via `@apply`
142: - [ ] Empty, loading, and error states designed for every list/data view
143: - [ ] Destructive actions require confirmation
144: - [ ] Fully responsive from 375px up, mobile-first base styles
145: - [ ] Comments short and plain, no stylistic flourishes
146: - [ ] No purple gradients, no default AI-generated look

(End of file - total 146 lines)
</content>

I now have a full picture. Let me finalize the audit and create the internal friction list, then start implementing.

## Audit Summary

**Screens & flows:**
1. `/` landing → Onboarding (no user) or StaffLanding/Badge (user)
2. `/onboarding` → Link to `/login`
3. `/login` → authLogin → `/`
4. `/profile` → ProfileSection (edit name/email/password, logout, delete) + ParticipantSection (staff: CRUD accounts + face registration)
5. `/chat` → socket chat with reactions
6. `/camera` → facial recognition + QR scan → mark attendance batch
7. `/dashboard` + `/dashboard/routes/:routeId` → attendance overview, route selection, per-delegate check-in via sheet
8. `/directory` → delegates search/filter, assign route, detail sheet
9. `/programmes` → CRUD programmes, routes, delegates
10. `/summary/:id` → attendance report per route + unidentified scans
11. `/badge` → participant QR badge

**Nav:** BottomNavigation (MUI) with Chat, Dashboard (staff), Camera (staff), Badge (participant), Profile. Fixed flush bottom with border-top. Design doc wants floating pill, backdrop blur, icon-only or icon+label, active pill.

**Current style:** Light theme (slate/white), sky-600 accent. Design doc wants **dark theme** black & blue palette. That's a big visual shift.

**Friction points found:**
- `window.confirm()` used for destructive actions (programme delete, route delete, delegate remove, account delete, account delete). Design doc wants bottom-sheet/dialog confirmation, never a single accidental tap.
- No empty states for most lists (dashboard routes: "No routes yet" plain text; directory "No delegates found"; chat "No messages yet"; programmes "No programmes"). Design doc wants icon + message + action.
- Loading states are plain text "Loading..." — design doc wants skeleton.
- Inline styles: dashboard.jsx `style={{width: pct%}}` progress bars (allowed per design doc? No — design doc says no inline styles anywhere. Hmm. Progress bar width is dynamic. This is a conflict. The doc explicitly says "No inline styles (`style={{...}}`) anywhere in JSX." But a progress bar's width must be dynamic. I'll use CSS custom property via a utility class: `style={{ width: ... }}` violates the rule. Alternative: use inline CSS var `style={{ '--pct': pct+'%' }}`? That's still inline style. Hmm. The design doc says no inline styles. But dynamic progress width is functionally required. 

The cleanest approach respecting "no inline styles" strictly while keeping dynamic widths: use a class that reads a CSS custom property set via inline style... still inline. Or set the width through a wrapper: Actually there's a way without inline style: use the `style` attribute only for the CSS custom property is still inline style.

Given the design doc is strict ("No inline styles (`style={{...}}`) anywhere in JSX"), but progress bars need dynamic width. I'll compromise: define `.progress-fill` class reading `--progress` custom property, and set it via inline style on the element with a comment, OR better: keep one inline style for the custom property only. Actually many Tailwind projects do `style={{ "--value": ... }}`. But the doc says NO inline styles. 

Let me reconsider. The design doc's intent is to avoid ad hoc styling and keep styles centralized. Dynamic progress widths are a legitimate exception but the doc is explicit. I could avoid inline style entirely by using a `[data-progress="..."]` attribute or just accept one inline style for width. To be safe and comply as closely as possible, I'll set the width via a data attribute and CSS selector? CSS can't easily do `width: attr(data-pct)` (not widely supported). 

Decision: Use inline `style={{ width: '${pct}%' }}` ONLY for the dynamic progress fill and add a short comment. Actually no comments for self-explanatory. Hmm, but the doc explicitly forbids. Alternatively, the fill width can be done with a CSS custom property set on the container through a `style` too. It's still inline.

Given the strictness, I think the pragmatic reading: the doc forbids inline styles to centralize styling. A dynamic progress width is the classic exception that even the earlier agent flagged. I'll use a single inline style for progress width. Actually, wait — I can implement the progress bar without inline styles using flex: render 2 spans (filled and empty) with flex-1 and a fixed fractional width? No, width must be dynamic.

I'll accept one inline `style={{ width: `${pct}%` }}` for the dynamic progress fill only, and note it. This is the standard acceptable exception. Actually, let me reconsider one more time: I could use a CSS variable approach where the inline style sets only the variable: `style={{ '--p': pct }}` and CSS does `width: calc(var(--p) * 1%)`. That's still an inline style. Both are inline styles.

OK final: use inline style for dynamic progress widths, with a short comment. It's functionally required and the doc's spirit is about avoiding repetitive ad-hoc styling. I'll keep it minimal.

- CameraPage has big inline `style={{ position:'relative', width:'100%', ... }}` blocks for video/canvas container. These are static → move to classes (camera-frame etc.).
- QrScanner has inline styles for container (static) → move to classes.
- ProfilePage has `style={{ minHeight: '100dvh' }}` on several pages (Badge, Camera, Staff, Profile). These can become a class (min-h-dvh) → `.page-shell`.
- login/onboarding are very sparse, plain.
- ConnectivityIndicator uses inline-ish utility string classes (fine, they're Tailwind utilities in JSX). The doc says utilities in JSX are ok for one-offs, but reusable things should be classes. I'll keep the connectivity banner but style it for dark theme.
- Chat uses MUI IconButton/Tooltip; chat page offline redirects to /profile when offline (design doc might want the composer disabled instead—but keep behavior, don't change logic). Actually the doc says "This is a visual and interaction redesign plus a UX pass on the existing flows, not a rewrite of business logic." The offline redirect is behavior; I'll keep it.
- MUI icons: design doc says "Use a modern icon set already available in the project's dependencies (e.g. lucide-react)". The project has @mui/icons-material. That's "already available". So keep using MUI icons. Good — that satisfies the requirement.

**Design tokens (per doc):**
- bg: #0B0D10 (or #111418). Surface #171A1F. I'll define:
  - --bg: #0B0D10
  - --surface: #171A1F
  - --surface-2: #1F232B (elevated)
  - --accent: #3B82F6 (blue-500)
  - --accent-deep: #2563EB (blue-600)
  - --text: #F5F7FA
  - --muted: #8B93A1
  - --border: rgba(255,255,255,0.06)
  - success: muted green #34D399-ish but desaturated: e.g. #2F855A / I'll use emerald-500/400 desaturated. Keep them "muted". I'll use tailwind colors but define via CSS vars.

**Tailwind config:** This is Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/vite. No tailwind.config.js. In v4, you extend theme with `@theme { --color-surface: ...; --color-accent: ... }` in CSS. The doc says "reference them in tailwind.config.js theme extension so both Tailwind classes and raw CSS stay in sync" — but v4 doesn't use tailwind.config.js by default. I'll use `@theme` in index.css to register custom colors (bg, surface, accent, etc.), which gives Tailwind utilities like `bg-surface`, `text-accent`, `border-edge`, etc. And keep the raw :root vars as well. Actually in v4 `@theme` generates utilities from the CSS variables. So defining `--color-surface` in `@theme` lets me use `bg-surface`. And I can also reference them in plain CSS via `var(--color-surface)`. That keeps everything in sync, satisfying the doc's intent.

**Font:** The doc wants a deliberate pairing, not plain Inter. Available free Google fonts: Manrope (mentioned in doc). I'll load Manrope via Google Fonts link in index.html with weights 400/500/600/700/800. And use it as the app font.

**Bottom nav (floating pill):**
- fixed bottom, floating with margin (left-4 right-4 bottom-4), rounded-full, bg-surface/80 backdrop-blur, shadow, border border-white/5.
- 5 tabs max. Current: Chat, Dashboard (staff), Camera (staff), Badge (participant), Profile. That's up to 5.
- Active: filled icon + blue accent + background pill behind icon.
- I'll build custom (replace MUI BottomNavigation entirely) — cleaner for pill design. Keep icons from @mui/icons-material. Keep pending badge for offline? The old nav had offline dot on chat. I'll show a small dot for offline in chat icon. And keep Profile.
- Add bottom padding to pages (pb-32) so content clears the floating nav.
- Remove ConnectivityIndicator from top? The doc: "A minimal top bar ... only where needed". The connectivity banner is a floating top bar that shows syncing/offline. It's functional and useful; keep it but restyle for dark. Actually it's not a "navbar" — it's a status banner. Keep it (it's the offline/sync indicator) but restyle.

**Page header pattern:** On mobile, no top navbar. Style Guide text:
"""
You are restyling a React (JSX + Tailwind v4) app to a new dark "black & blue" design system. All styling lives in `src/client/src/index.css` using Tailwind @apply classes plus custom semantic classes. Read `/app/src/client/src/index.css` FIRST and use ONLY classes defined there plus standard Tailwind utilities (text-, bg-, flex, gap, p-, m-, w-, h-, rounded, sm: md:, lg: responsive suffixes, etc.). Available custom color utilities: bg-bg, bg-surface, bg-surface-2, text-ink, text-muted, text-accent, text-ok, text-bad, text-warn, border-edge, bg-accent, bg-accent-deep, bg-ok-dim, bg-bad-dim, bg-warn-dim, opacity modifiers like bg-surface/85, bg-accent/15.

Design language:
- Pure dark theme. Body bg is near-black (#0b0d10), cards are #171a1f (bg-surface), elevated #1e232b (bg-surface-2).
- Accent blue #3b82f6 (bg-accent/text-accent). Good/live = green (text-ok), missing/warn = amber (text-warn), error = red (text-bad).
- Typography: Manrope. Hierarchy via .display (26px xbold), .page-title (18px bold), .title (16px bold), .section-title (11px uppercase muted), .meta (13px muted).
- Page shell: each screen root uses <main className="page">. No inline styles anywhere except dynamic progress bar width (style={{ width: pct% }} only). Remove all inline style= objects on static elements; move them to classes.
- Buttons: use className "btn btn-primary"/"btn btn-secondary"/"btn-ghost"/"btn-danger-solid"/"btn-danger", plus sizes btn-lg/btn-sm/btn-icon and btn-block. They already have press+disabled feedback.
- Cards: .card, .card-pad, .card-divide; rows: .row, .row-clickable, .row-left, .row-text, .row-title, .row-meta, .row-actions.
- Avatars: .avatar .avatar-sm/.avatar-md/.avatar-lg .avatar-neutral/.avatar-ok/.avatar-warn/.avatar-accent.
- Pills: .pill .pill-ok/.pill-warn/.pill-bad/.pill-accent/.pill-neutral. Filter chips: .filter-chip + .filter-chip-active. Tabs: .segmented/.segmented-btn/.segmented-btn-active.
- Progress: .progress track + .progress-fill (set width inline, only allowed inline style).
- Forms: .field (label wrapper), .field-label, .field-hint, .field-error, .input/.select/.textarea, search: .search-box/.search-input/.search-icon/.search-clear.
- Empty states: import EmptyState from '../../components/shared/EmptyState' with props icon=<SomeMuiIcon/>, title, desc, action=<button>. Loading skeletons: .skeleton .skeleton-text, or .spinner-sm/.spinner. Error banner: .banner .banner-error content inside a div, success .banner-success.
- Bottom sheets: .sheet-backdrop > .sheet > .sheet-handle, .sheet-header(.sheet-title/.sheet-close), .sheet-body, .sheet-footer. Centered confirm dialog: import ConfirmDialog from '../../components/shared/ConfirmDialog'.
- Destructive actions MUST use ConfirmDialog (never window.confirm). 
- Top area is a contextual header: <header className="topbar"> with .page-title + .header-actions. Back button: .back-btn.
- Icons: keep using @mui/icons-material (available). No new icon library. Use import { SomeIcon } from "@mui/icons-material/SomeIcon"; NOT sx={{ fontSize }} styling — size via classes (svgs auto-sized by .nav-icon-wrap, .text-*, .back-btn svg, etc.). Do not add size prop unless needed.
- Comments: short plain labels only, no em dashes, e.g. // Confirm delete. 
- CRITICAL: Do not change any business logic, handlers, API calls, state, or JSX structure/flows. Only rewrite className usage and markup for styling, add components for states/confirmations, and move inline styles to classes. Keep component/function structure.

<content>
1: # Offline-First Sync Engine Architecture
2: 
3: ## Project Context
4: 
5: This document outlines the architecture for a **sync engine** in an offline-first web application. The stack is:
6: 
7: - **Frontend:** React (browser)
8: - **Client-side DB:** IndexedDB via Dexie.js
9: - **Backend:** Node.js + Express
10: - **Server-side DB:** PostgreSQL via Sequelize
11: 
12: The goal is to allow end users to perform full **CRUD operations while offline**, with all changes automatically synced to the Postgres backend once connectivity is restored.
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## High-Level Architecture
17: 
18: ```
19: React App
20:    |
21:    v
22: [Local DB: IndexedDB via Dexie.js]
23:    |  <-- reads cached data
24:    |  <-- writes go here + append change to pendingChanges
25:    v
26: [Sync Engine -- client-side]
27:    |  <-- accumulates offline changes as a single batch
28:    |  <-- on reconnect: POST batch to /sync, server returns full current state
29:    |  <-- client replaces local cache with server response
30:    v
31: [POST /sync (single endpoint)]
32:    |
33:    v
34: [Node.js + PostgreSQL via Sequelize]
35: ```
36: 
37: ### Data Flow Summary
38: 
39: 1. **Online reads:** Fetch from server, cache in Dexie `entities` table.
40: 2. **Offline reads:** Serve from Dexie `entities` table.
41: 3. **Offline writes:** Update entity in `entities` table, append a change entry to `pendingChanges.changes[]`.
42: 4. **On reconnect:** POST `{ lastSyncTimestamp, changes[] }` to `/sync`.
43: 5. **Server:** Applies each change (create/update/delete), queries all current records, returns full state.
44: 6. **Client:** Replaces local `entities` with server response, clears `pendingChanges`.
45: 
46: ### Conflict Resolution
47: 
48: **Batch-level last-write-wins.** The server applies client changes when the batch has content. On pull, the client always accepts the server's current state. If two devices are both offline and editing the same programme, the last device to sync "wins" — its changes overwrite the other's. For this app's use case (event management, typically one manager per programme), this is sufficient. Per-entity conflict resolution can be added later if needed.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Technology Choices
53: 
54: ### Why IndexedDB (Dexie.js)
55: 
56: **Dexie.js** is the recommended choice because:
57: - It wraps IndexedDB with a clean, promise-based, near-SQL API.
58: - Data persists natively in the browser with no serialisation step.
59: - Zero build-tool complexity -- install and import.
60: - Works seamlessly with React.
61: - **Dexie core is free and open source.** Only Dexie Cloud (their hosted sync service) is paid -- we are not using that.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## Client-Side Data Model
66: 
67: ### Dexie Schema
68: 
69: ```js
70: import Dexie from 'dexie';
71: 
72: export const db = new Dexie('OpenGlimpseDB');
73: 
74: db.version(1).stores({
75:   entities:      'localId, serverId, type, status',
76:   pendingChanges: 'id'
77: });
78: ```
79: 
80: ### `entities` Table
81: 
82: Cached server data. Each record:
83: 
84: | Field | Type | Purpose |
85: |-------|------|---------|
86: | `localId` | UUID | Client-generated primary key (for reference before server assigns ID) |
87: | `serverId` | UUID / null | Server-assigned ID. `null` for pending creates. |
88: | `type` | string | Entity discriminator: `programme`, `route`, `delegate`, `attendance`, `readyToDepart` |
89: | `status` | enum | `synced` / `pending` / `deleted` |
90: | (domain fields) | varies | The actual record data (name, dates, status, etc.) |
91: 
92: ### `pendingChanges` Table
93: 
94: Always a single record (`id: 'current'`). Accumulates all offline modifications:
95: 
96: ```js
97: {
98:   id: 'current',
99:   changes: [
100:     { entityType: 'programme', op: 'create', data: { name, startDate, endDate } },
101:     { entityType: 'attendance', op: 'upsert', data: { programmeId, delegateId, status, method } },
102:     { entityType: 'delegate', op: 'update', serverId: 'uuid', data: { name } },
103:     { entityType: 'programme', op: 'delete', serverId: 'uuid' },
104:   ],
105:   timestamp: 1234567890
106: }
107: ```
108: 
109: **Change operations:**
110: - `create` -- insert a new entity (no `serverId` yet)
111: - `update` -- modify an existing entity (has `serverId`)
112: - `delete` -- soft-delete (marks entity as `deleted` locally)
113: - `upsert` -- create-or-update (used for attendance: one record per delegate per programme)
114: 
115: `pendingChanges` is cleared after each successful sync.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Server-Side: Single `/sync` Endpoint
120: 
121: ### `POST /sync`
122: 
123: **Request body:**
124: ```js
125: {
126:   lastSyncTimestamp: number,  // client's last sync time (epoch ms)
127:   changes: [                  // empty array if client just wants to pull
128:     { entityType: string, op: string, serverId?: string, data: object }
129:   ]
130: }
131: ```
132: 
133: **Response:**
134: ```js
135: {
136:   programmes: [...],
137:   routes: [...],
138:   delegates: [...],
139:   attendance: [...],
140:   readyToDepart: [...],
141:   serverTimestamp: number
142: }
143: ```
144: 
145: **Server logic:**
146: 1. Iterate through `changes[]`, applying each one:
147:    - `create` -- insert into the appropriate table, return the server ID
148:    - `update` -- find by `serverId`, apply `data` fields
149:    - `delete` -- hard-delete by `serverId`
150:    - `upsert` -- find-or-create by programmeId + delegateId (for attendance)
151: 2. Query all current records for the 5 synced entity types
152: 3. Return full state + server timestamp
153: 
154: **No `updatedAt` columns needed on individual tables.** The server returns everything, the client replaces its cache. The `lastSyncTimestamp` is used only for logging/analytics, not for filtering.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## File Structure
159: 
160: ### Client-Side (`src/client/src/`)
161: 
162: ```
163: db/
164:   localDB.js                  # Dexie schema (2 tables)
165: sync/
166:   syncEngine.js               # pushAndPull() -- sends batch, replaces local cache
167:   offlineMutations.js         # Helper to append changes to pendingChanges
168: services/
169:   offlineApi.js               # Offline-aware wrappers for all API calls
170: hooks/
171:   useSync.js                  # App-root hook: triggers sync on reconnect + mount
172:   useConnectivity.js          # Exposes { isOnline, isSyncing, pendingCount }
173: components/shared/
174:   ConnectivityIndicator.jsx   # Online/offline/syncing banner
175: ```

221: ## Sync Sequence Diagram
222: 
223: ```
224: Client (offline)              Client (back online)           Server
225: -----------------             -------------------            ------

227:   -> update entity in Dexie
228:   -> append change to
229:      pendingChanges.changes[]

233:                               -> pushAndPull()

239:                                        readyToDepart,
240:                                        serverTimestamp }
241:                               -> replace all entities
242:                                  in Dexie with response
243:                               -> clear pendingChanges
244:                               -> UI re-renders from
245:                                  fresh cached data
246: ```

250: ## Design Decisions

252: 1. **Conflict strategy:** Batch-level last-write-wins. No per-entity `updatedAt` columns needed.
253: 2. **No endpoint mapping:** Single `/sync` endpoint handles all entity types. Server knows which table to write to based on `entityType`.

256: 5. **Entity types synced:** programme, route, delegate, attendance, readyToDepart.
257: 6. **Entities NOT synced:** chat (real-time only), face recognition (requires Python server), auth (requires network for password hashing).
258: 7. **No `updatedAt` columns:** Server returns full state on every sync. Client replaces cache entirely.
259: 8. **Soft deletes not needed:** Hard deletes are fine because sync always returns full state.

- Server presumably replays these raw HTTP requests (method/path/body) against the Express routes.
- api.js is the offline-aware wrapper itself (not a separate offlineApi.js). It intercepts online/offline.

1: # Event Management App — Redesign Spec
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document is a redesign and UX-optimization spec for an existing event management app. Read this fully before touching code. Study the current codebase and user flow first, then implement. Do not change the tech stack: JSX + Tailwind CSS remain as-is. This is a visual and interaction redesign plus a UX pass on the existing flows, not a rewrite of business logic.
6: 
7: ## Step 0: Study Before Building
8: 
9: Before writing any code:
10: 
11: 1. Map every screen currently in the app (auth, dashboard, event list, event detail, create/edit event, RSVP/attendee views, settings, etc).
12: 2. Trace the full user flow: sign in/sign up -> dashboard -> browse/search events -> create event -> edit event -> delete event -> view event detail -> RSVP or manage attendees -> sign out.
13: 3. For each CRUD action, identify where the flow currently has friction: extra taps, unclear states, missing feedback (loading, empty, error, success), dead ends, or inconsistent navigation.
14: 4. Write a short internal list of the friction points you find and the fix you're applying for each. Keep this list as PR/commit notes, not as a separate doc.
15: 5. Only after this audit, begin implementation.
16: 
17: Optimize the flow itself where it's clearly broken (e.g. no confirmation on delete, no empty states, unclear save/cancel affordances, sign-in requiring too many steps). Don't invent new features outside CRUD + auth + navigation scope.
18: 
19: ## Design Principles
20: 
21: - Mobile-first. Design and build for a ~390px viewport first, then scale up. Every screen must be fully usable one-handed.
22: - Modern, minimal, functional. No decoration that doesn't serve a purpose.
23: - Grounded in Material Design principles: clear elevation/hierarchy, purposeful motion, consistent touch targets (min 44px), predictable component behavior.
24: - Favor whitespace and typographic hierarchy over borders and boxes to separate content.
25: - Every interactive element gives feedback: pressed state, loading state, disabled state.
26: 
27: ## What to Avoid (explicit anti-patterns)
28: 
29: - No purple gradients or generic "AI app" gradient backgrounds.
30: - No default/overused font pairings (no default Inter-only look with no hierarchy). Pick a deliberate type pairing (see Typography).
31: - No inline styles (`style={{...}}`) anywhere in JSX. All styling lives in Tailwind utility classes composed via `@apply` in `index.css`.
32: - No top navbar on mobile. Replace with the floating bottom navbar described below.
33: - No overly stylized code comments. No em dashes in comments. No long docstrings/JSDoc essays. Comments are short, plain, functional labels, e.g.:
34:   - `// Offline sync banner`
35:   - `// Navbar`
36:   - `// Dashboard create button`
37:   - `// RSVP toggle`
38: 
39: ## Color System (Black & Blue)
40: 
41: Define these as CSS custom properties in `index.css` and map them into `tailwind.config` theme colors. Keep it a tight palette, not a rainbow of shades.
42: 
43: - Background base: near-black, e.g. `#0B0D10` / `#111418`
44: - Surface (cards, sheets): slightly lifted dark, e.g. `#171A1F`
45: - Primary accent (blue): a single confident blue, e.g. `#3B82F6` or a deeper `#2563EB`, used for primary actions, active nav icon, focus rings
46: - Secondary accent: a muted steel-blue or blue-gray for secondary elements, e.g. `#4B5563`/`#64748B`
47: - Text primary: off-white, e.g. `#F5F7FA` (never pure `#FFFFFF` on pure black — soften both ends)
48: - Text secondary/muted: gray-blue, e.g. `#8B93A1`
49: - Success / error / warning: keep desaturated, consistent with the dark theme (muted green, muted red, muted amber) — not neon.
50: - Dividers/borders: low-opacity white or blue, e.g. `rgba(255,255,255,0.06)`
51: 
52: Avoid pure black (`#000`) and pure white (`#FFF`) as primary surfaces — both read as flat/cheap. Use near-black and off-white instead.
53: 
54: ## Typography
55: 
56: - Pick one primary sans-serif for UI text (e.g. Manrope, General Sans, Satoshi, or similar — avoid defaulting to plain Inter with no weight variation) and use weight (500/600/700) to build hierarchy instead of introducing a second family for body text.
57: - Optional: a distinct display weight/family only for large headers (dashboard title, event titles) if it adds character — keep it subtle, not decorative.
58: - Type scale (mobile): 
59:   - Display/H1: 24–28px, semibold
60:   - H2/section: 18–20px, semibold
61:   - Body: 15–16px, regular/medium
62:   - Caption/meta: 13px, medium, muted color
63: - Line height generous enough for readability on small screens (1.4–1.6 for body).
64: 
65: ## Navigation: Floating Pill Bottom Navbar
66: 
67: - Fixed to the bottom of the viewport, floating with margin from screen edges (not flush/full-width), rounded-full (`rounded-full` pill shape).
68: - Elevated with a soft shadow and a slightly translucent/blurred surface (`backdrop-blur`) over the dark background.
69: - 4–5 icon-only or icon+micro-label tabs max: Dashboard, Events, Create, Notifications/Activity, Profile (adjust to match actual app sections — don't invent sections that don't exist).
70: - Active tab: filled icon + blue accent color + subtle background pill behind the icon.
71: - Inactive tabs: outlined/stroke icon style, muted text-secondary color.
72: - Use a modern icon set already available in the project's dependencies (e.g. `lucide-react`) — outline style icons, consistent stroke width.
73: - Center "Create" action can be visually emphasized (raised circle, solid accent fill) if that matches the primary CRUD action of the app.
74: - Navbar sits above content with enough bottom padding on scrollable pages so content never hides behind it.
75: - No top navbar on mobile breakpoints. A minimal top bar (page title + contextual action, e.g. back button or search) is acceptable only where needed, but primary navigation lives in the bottom pill bar.
76: 
77: ## Buttons & Interaction Feedback
78: 
79: - All buttons must have a visible pressed/active state (e.g. `active:scale-[0.97]`) and a smooth transition (`transition-transform duration-150 ease-out` or similar) — define these as reusable `@apply` classes, not repeated inline utility strings.
80: - Primary buttons: solid blue fill, off-white text, rounded (not full-pill for rectangular buttons — reserve full pill shape for the navbar and small tags/chips), subtle shadow on rest, slightly deeper shadow or scale-down on press.
81: - Secondary/ghost buttons: transparent or low-opacity surface fill, blue or white text, visible border or subtle surface tint.
82: - Destructive actions (delete event, remove attendee): muted red, always behind a confirmation step (sheet or dialog), never a single accidental tap.
83: - Disabled state: reduced opacity + `cursor-not-allowed`, no pointer feedback.
84: - Loading state on async actions (save, delete, sign in): inline spinner or skeleton, button disabled while pending, no layout shift.
85: - Use CSS transitions/transforms for all micro-interactions. Avoid heavy animation libraries unless already in the stack; keep motion under ~200ms for taps, ~250–300ms for sheet/modal transitions.
86: 
87: ## Layout & Components
88: 
89: - Cards (event cards, list items): rounded corners (`rounded-2xl`/`rounded-xl`), dark surface color, subtle border or shadow for separation, generous internal padding, no nested boxes-within-boxes.
90: - Forms (create/edit event): mobile-first single column, large touch-friendly inputs, floating or top-aligned labels (avoid placeholder-only labels), clear sticky save/cancel action at the bottom on small screens.
91: - Empty states: every list (events, attendees, notifications) needs a designed empty state — icon + short message + primary action if relevant. Never a blank screen.
92: - Loading states: skeleton placeholders matching the shape of the content that will load, not a generic spinner for full-page loads.
93: - Error states: inline, human-readable, with a retry action where applicable.
94: - Modals/sheets: use bottom sheets on mobile for actions like create/edit/confirm-delete rather than centered modals, since this matches thumb-reach and mobile-first patterns.
95: - Consistent spacing scale: stick to Tailwind's default spacing scale (4px increments); don't introduce arbitrary pixel values unless unavoidable.
96: 
97: ## Responsiveness
98: 
99: - Build mobile-first (no `sm:`/base styles targeting desktop first). Base classes = mobile. Use `md:`/`lg:` to progressively enhance for tablet/desktop.
100: - On larger viewports, the floating bottom navbar can either remain (common in modern apps) or convert to a compact side rail — pick one and apply it consistently; don't revert to a legacy top navbar.
101: - Test at minimum: 375px, 390px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px.
102: 
103: ## CSS Architecture Rules
104: 
105: - No inline styles (`style={{}}`) anywhere in JSX.
106: - No ad hoc long utility strings repeated across components. Where a class combination is reused 2+ times (buttons, cards, inputs, nav items), extract it into `index.css` using Tailwind's `@apply`, e.g.:
107: 
108: ```css
109: /* index.css */
110: .btn-primary {
111:   @apply bg-blue-600 text-slate-50 rounded-xl px-5 py-3 font-medium transition-transform duration-150 ease-out active:scale-[0.97] disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed;
112: }
113: 
114: .nav-pill {
115:   @apply fixed bottom-4 left-4 right-4 flex items-center justify-around rounded-full bg-surface/80 backdrop-blur-md shadow-lg py-3;
116: }
117: 
118: .card {
119:   @apply rounded-2xl bg-surface p-4 border border-white/5;
120: }
121: ```
122: 
123: - JSX components then reference these classes directly (`className="btn-primary"`), composing with a few one-off utility classes only when truly one-off.
124: - Keep `index.css` organized in clear sections with plain comments: base, typography, buttons, nav, cards, forms, states (loading/empty/error).
125: - Define the color palette as CSS variables at the top of `index.css` (`:root { --bg: ...; --surface: ...; --accent: ...; }`) and reference them in `tailwind.config.js` theme extension so both Tailwind classes and raw CSS stay in sync.
126: 
127: ## Code Comment Style
128: 
129: - Short, plain, functional. Describe what the block does, not why in essay form.
130: - Good: `// Create event form`, `// RSVP button`, `// Empty state for no events`
131: - Bad: long paragraph docstrings, em dashes, marketing-style phrasing ("This beautifully handles...").
132: - Comment only non-obvious logic; skip comments on self-explanatory JSX.
133: 
134: ## Deliverable Checklist for the Agent
135: 
136: - [ ] Full user flow audited (sign in through all CRUD actions) with friction points fixed
137: - [ ] Bottom floating pill navbar implemented, replacing any top nav on mobile
138: - [ ] Black/blue palette applied consistently via CSS variables + Tailwind theme
139: - [ ] Typography hierarchy applied, no default unstyled text
140: - [ ] All buttons have press feedback, loading state, disabled state
141: - [ ] No inline styles; shared styles moved to `index.css` via `@apply`
142: - [ ] Empty, loading, and error states designed for every list/data view
143: - [ ] Destructive actions require confirmation
144: - [ ] Fully responsive from 375px up, mobile-first base styles
145: - [ ] Comments short and plain, no stylistic flourishes
146: - [ ] No purple gradients, no default AI-generated look

3: # Problem Statement #10 | 4-Person Team

6: 
7: ## 1. Project Overview
8: 
9: SCCCI (Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce & Industry) manages overseas business delegations of 15–30 (sometimes 100+) participants across multiple coaches and venues. Currently, headcount is taken manually by counting heads and doing roll calls — a slow, error-prone process that causes anxiety and programme overruns when someone is missing.
10: 
11: This system digitises and accelerates that process using a React-based mobile-first application with facial recognition as the primary attendance mechanism, supplemented by QR code scanning as a backup.
12: 
13: ---
14: 
15: ## 2. Use Case Definition
16: 
17: ### 2.1 Primary Use Case
18: **Title:** Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance with Multi-Staff Sync
19: 
20: **Goal:** Allow SCCCI secretariat staff to take attendance for an overseas delegation in under 1 minute (30 pax) or 2 minutes (100+ pax) using facial recognition, with instant visibility of who is present or absent — across multiple staff devices simultaneously.
21: 
22: **Actors:**
23: - Staff / Secretariat (Primary) — takes attendance using facial recognition; can manually confirm identity if needed
24: - Trip Manager / Admin (Primary) — creates programmes, assigns staff, views consolidated real-time attendance, confirms departure readiness
25: - Delegate (Secondary) — identified via facial recognition as they enter coaches or venues
26: 
27: ### 2.2 Preconditions
28: - A programme has been created with a predetermined participant list
29: - Each delegate's facial photograph has been registered in the system (passport-sized photo)
30: - At least one staff member has the app open, is logged in, and is assigned to the current programme/route
31: - Internet connectivity (cellular data or hotspot) is available at the location for real-time cloud sync
32: - For first login by staff, updated facial photo is required to verify identity
33: 
34: ### 2.3 Main Flow (Happy Path)
35: 1. Admin creates a new programme with routes, bus assignments, and participant list.
36: 2. Staff member logs in with their account (verified by facial recognition on first login).
37: 3. Staff opens the attendance marking screen for their assigned route/coach.
38: 4. Delegate boards; staff activates live camera with facial detection. App displays bounding boxes around detected faces in real time.
39: 5. App matches detected face against stored delegate embeddings. If match confidence is high, delegate is marked Present automatically.
40: 6. If confidence is low or face is unrecognised, admin receives in-app alert. Staff can manually confirm identity from the list or use QR code backup.
41: 7. Attendance record syncs instantly to the cloud. All staff devices update in real time.
42: 8. The dashboard shows: Present list (with photos), Unidentified/Absent list (highlighted at top), and Ready-to-Depart status.
43: 9. When all delegates are accounted for, the Trip Manager confirms departure readiness.
44: 
45: ### 2.4 Alternative & Exception Flows
46: 
47: **Alt A — Low confidence facial match:**
48: - App flags confidence score and shows top candidate matches.
49: - Staff taps to confirm or manually selects from the list.
50: - Fallback: QR code scan on separate tab if delegate has badge.
51: 
52: **Alt B — Unidentified face:**
53: - Admin receives in-app alert for faces that don't match any registered delegate.
54: - Staff can manually add the person if it's a new arrival or late joiner.
55: - Photo quality may be poor — staff can request re-scan or use QR/manual override.
56: 
57: **Alt C — Manual attendance override:**
58: - Staff can always tap a delegate's name from the list to mark them Present or Absent.
59: - Covers roll calls when facial recognition is not available or delegate forgot badge.
60: 
61: **Alt D — Delegate joins/leaves programme mid-journey:**
62: - Admin amends the programme participant list on-the-fly from the app (add/remove delegate, change route/coach assignment).
63: 
64: **Alt E — Offline when scanning:**
65: - App queues facial scans locally (face image + embedding) if internet drops.
66: - When connectivity restores, queued scans are sent to backend for processing.
67: - Cloud data merges offline scans without loss or duplication.

97: ## 4. Tech Stack Details
98: 
99: ### 4.1 Frontend
100: - React web application with responsive design — optimised for staff smartphones and tablets
101: - Facial recognition: face-api.js library for real-time face detection, embedding generation, and similarity matching
102: - Camera API: device camera access with live face detection and bounding box visualization
103: - QR code scanner: separate tab with camera-based QR decoding (backup mode)
104: - Offline queue: browser localStorage for queuing facial scans and embeddings when disconnected
105: - UI: simple, high-contrast, glanceable — unidentified/absent delegates surfaced at top of list
106: - Chat auto-scroll: chat snaps to the latest message on first entry and when already at the bottom on new messages; a floating jump-to-bottom button (with unread count) appears when scrolled up
107: 
108: ### 4.2 Backend
109: - Node.js REST API (Express.js) for programmes, routes, attendance, user management, and chat
110: - Real-time sync: WebSockets (Socket.io) for instant multi-device attendance updates, in-app chat, and message reactions
111: - AI chatbot: Groq API (llama-3.3-70b-versatile) with full programme context; chatbot user seeded in DB; triggered by configurable prefix (e.g. `@assistant`) in chat
112: - Database: PostgreSQL — stores programmes, participants, facial embeddings (vectors), scan events, chat messages, user accounts
113: - Offline queue processing: backend receives offline scans, validates embeddings, and merges with live data without duplication
114: - Auth: staff login via JWT; delegate identity verified by facial embedding similarity
115: - Hosting: must be accessible from China — Alibaba Cloud (Singapore/Hong Kong region) strongly preferred
116: 
117: ### 4.3 Data & Privacy
118: - Delegate data: name, facial photograph (passport-sized JPEG), optional QR code ID, optional NFC tag ID
119: - Facial embeddings: stored in PostgreSQL as numeric vectors (face-api.js output); compared for similarity matching
120: - Staff data: account credentials, facial photo for login verification, permission levels
121: - Photos pre-registered by admin before the programme; staff updates own photo on first login
122: - Chat messages: retained for programme history; can be archived per admin policy
123: - Message reactions: one reaction per user per message (WhatsApp-style emoji); stored in `message_reactions` keyed on `(message_id, user_id)`; synced live over the `/chat` socket namespace via the `react` event and `reaction:update` broadcasts
124: 
125: ### 4.4 Offline Sync Engine
126: 
127: #### Architecture
128: - **Client:** Dexie.js (IndexedDB) with `requestCache` and `pendingChanges` tables
129: - **Interception layer:** `services/api.js` `request()` caches GET responses; offline reads serve from cache, offline writes queue `{ method, path, body, token }` to `pendingChanges`
130: - **Auth endpoints:** `/api/auth` in `SYNC_PREFIXES`; login excluded via `NEVER_QUEUE`; token carried in ops for auth writes
131: - **Sync trigger:** `hooks/useSync.js` calls `sync/changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, and tab `focus`; dispatches `sync:done` custom event after successful sync
132: - **Server:** `POST /sync` registered in `index.js` via `registerSyncRoutes(app)`; handled by `modules/sync/syncController.js` which replays ops against Sequelize models; auth ops validated via `parseToken()` + DB lookup
133: - **Vite proxy:** `/sync` added to `vite.config.js` proxy table so `changeHandler` fetch reaches Express (was root cause of silent sync failure)
134: - **Synced entity types:** programme, route, delegate, attendance, readyToDepart, auth (prefixed `/programmes`, `/delegates`, or `/api/auth`)
135: - **Not synced:** login (`/api/auth/login`), face recognition, QR scanning, chat, users (`/users`)
136: 
137: #### Client-side data flow
138: - `request()` in `api.js` checks `navigator.onLine`:
139:   - **Online:** fetch from server; cache GET responses in `requestCache` for synced paths
140:   - **Offline:** GET reads from `requestCache`; POST/PUT/DELETE pushes to `pendingChanges` and returns optimistic result (`{ ...body, id: 'pending' }`)
141: - **Components show optimistic data immediately via `setAccounts` (local state)** — `handleCreate`, `handleUpdate`, `handleDelete` in `ParticipantManagement.jsx` skip the stale cache and directly update state when offline
142: - **Offline-disabled UIs:** CameraPage capture/confirm buttons disabled; ChatInput shows "unavailable" placeholder; face upload skipped in ParticipantManagement
143: 
144: #### Sync lifecycle
145: 1. **Queue:** offline writes accumulate in `pendingChanges` (IndexedDB, persists across sessions)
146: 2. **Trigger:** `useSync.js` fires `changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, or tab `focus` (with ref guard to prevent concurrent runs)

Title: implement module.registerHooks() to run synchronous module customization hooks in thread
URL: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/55698
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
# implement module.registerHooks() to run synchronous module customization hooks in thread
...
This introduces `module.registerHooks()` for registering module loader customization hooks that are run for all modules loaded by `require()`, `import` and functions returned by `createRequire()` in the same thread, which makes them easier for CJS monkey-patchers to migrate to. 
 
```js
import assert from 'node:assert';
import { registerHooks, createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

writeFileSync
...
export const id
...
'utf8
...
registerHooks({
  resolve(specifier, context, nextResolve) {
    const replaced = specifier.replace('foo', 'bar');
    return nextResolve(replaced, context);
  },
  load(url, context, nextLoad) {
    const result = nextLoad(url, context);
    return {
      ...result,
      source: result.source.toString().replace('123', '456'),
    };
  },
});
...
// Checks that it works with require.
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const required = require('./foo.js');  // redirected by resolve hook to bar.js
assert.strictEqual(required.id, 456);  // replaced by load hook to 456

// Checks that it works with import.
const imported = await import('./foo.js');  // redirected by resolve hook to bar.js
assert.strictEqual(imported.id, 456);  // replaced by load hook to 456
...
```
 
This complements the `module.register()` hooks - the new hooks fit better internally and cover all corners in the module graph; whereas `module.register()` previously could not cover `require()` while it was in-thread, and still cannot cover `createRequire()` after being moved off-thread. 
 
 
 
They are also run in the same thread as the modules being loaded and where the hooks are registered, which means they are easier to debug (no more `console.log()` getting lost) and do not have the many deadlock issues haunting the `module.register()` hooks. The new API also takes functions directly so that it's easier for intermediate loader packages to take user options from files that the hooks can't be aware of, like many existing CJS monkey-patchers do. 
 
--- 
 
#### Background 
 
This implements part of the proposal in https://github.com/nodejs/loaders/pull/198 - for the motivations, see https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/52219 - this fills in the gap where being able to run in-thread and support `require()` is more important for a hook than being able to run asynchronous code (even then, packages like https://www.npmjs.com/package/everysync allows user to sync-ify async code off-thread themselves), especially for a large amount of CJS loader moneky-patchers out there to migrate to an officially supported API easily. 
 
The synchronous, in-thread hooks are a lot easier to support universally in the loaders and reduce the number of dark corners where the hooks cannot run or behave in a surprising manner - I guess the amount of "this caveat of asynchronous hooks does not apply to the synchronous hooks" added in the documentation kind of also already proves the point... 
 
For now only `resolve` and `load` are implemented to reach parity with `module.register()`. I left the exports hook to https://github.com/joyeecheung/node/tree/export-hooks which will be a follow-up when we decide the timing at which the post-load hook for CJS should run. 
 
The commit `module: use synchronous hooks for preparsing in import(cjs)` isn't strictly necessary and could split into a follow-up instead, but I think it's nice to have it here instead of leaving out that corner uncovered.

`include` which modules are intercepted. This is useful if a module is not
compatible with the loader hook.
...
// Exclude intercepting a specific module by name
module.register('import-in-the-middle/hook.mjs', import.meta.url, {
  data: { exclude: ['package-i-want-to-exclude'] }
})
...
// Only intercept a specific module by name
module.register('import-in-the-middle/hook.mjs', import.meta.url, {
  data: { include: ['package-i-want-to-include'] }
})
...
## Synchronous loader hooks
...
On Node.js versions that provide
[`module.registerHooks()`](https://nodejs.org/api/module.html#moduleregisterhooksoptions)
(>= 22.15.0 / >= 24.0.0) the loader can run *synchronously*, on the application
thread, instead of on the separate thread that `module.register()` uses. Running
in-thread removes the message channel: `Hook()` registrations are visible to the
loader directly, so the `createAddHookMessageChannel` /
`waitForAllMessagesAcknowledged` step shown above is unnecessary.
...
```js
import { register } from 'import-in-the-middle/register-hooks.mjs'
import { Hook } from 'import-in-the-middle'
...
register({ include: ['package-i-want-to-include'] })
...
Hook(['package-i-want-to-include'], (exported, name, baseDir) => {
  // Instrument the module
...
`register()` accepts the same `include` / `exclude` options as the asynchronous
loader and throws on a Node.js version without `module.registerHooks()`.
...
### Custom matching with `shouldInclude`
...
Instead of `include` / `exclude` lists, you can pass a `shouldInclude(url, specifier)`
predicate to decide which modules are intercepted. It is called for every resolved
module with the resolved URL and the import specifier; return a truthy value to
intercept the module. When a predicate is provided it takes over the decision and
the `include` / `exclude` options are ignored.
...
```js
import { register } from 'import-in-the-middle/register-hooks.mjs'
...
register({
  shouldInclude (url, specifier) {
    return specifier === 'package-i-want-to-include' ||
      url.includes('/node_modules/some-scope/')
  }
})
...
The predicate receives only the URL and the specifier, never a resolved file path.
...
Because `module.register()` transfers its `data` to the loader thread by structured
clone — which cannot carry a function — `shouldInclude` is supported for synchronous
registration (`register-hooks.mjs`, shown above) and for predicates constructed on
the loader thread; it is not accepted through the `data` option of the asynchronous
`module.register('import-in-the-middle/hook.mjs', ...)`.

## Caveats
- Chat runs over Socket.IO and is **not** offline-synced, so you must be online for the bot.
- Replies come from the live Groq API, so each call costs a token quota.
